newsitem.title: USA: U.S. meat export group to promote grass-fed beef.
newsitem.headline: U.S. meat export group to promote grass-fed beef.

text.p: The U.S. Meat Export Federation (USMEF) said it has organized an alliance of foreign buyers and U.S. meat packers and processors to market U.S. grass-fed beef around the world.
"The alliance will help us get our foot in the door and give us access to new market segments where we couldn't compete before," said Stephen Neel, USMEF director of technical services, in a release.
Customers are to include Russia, China, Taiwan, Korea, Indonesia, Mexico and the Caribbean. Also, South Africa, Eastern Europe and the European Union may be new markets.
Neel said the United States has an abundant supply of grass-fed beef which is about half the price of grain-fed beef.

In the case of the European Union, U.S. grass-fed cows are not treated with growth promotants as are used by some U.S. feedlots producing grain-fed beef. For that reason, grass-fed cattle sales would not be affected by the EU ban on beef produced with such promotants, he said.
Sales of grass-fed beef will not be applied to the EU's import quota of high-quality beef, which is 12,250 metric tons. As a result the EU may become an important market for this beef, Neel said.
In 1995, the United States produced 3.82 billion lbs of grass-fed beef, about 50 percent of which came from the dairy industry.
Cattle-Fax, a Denver-based cattle market advisory service, said grass-fed beef production may increase in 1996 and 1997 because the beef industry is in a herd liquidation phase.
The USMEF is a trade association which develops international markets for U.S. red meat products.
